disp8.4.stem: DISP8.4: Commencing court proceedings: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: The owner of an office block wishes to bring a claim against a sole trader decorator that used the wrong colour of paint. The colour they used is not consistent with the tenant’s brand and will have to be redone. The decorator has refused to admit their mistake. The owner estimates their losses at £80,000 plus legal costs of £45,000 which they will seek to recover from the decorator. Should the claim be issued in the County Court or the High Court?
options: High Court, because the sum claimed is over £50,000.
County Court, because the claim is against an individual.
High Court, because the sum claimed is over £100,000.
County Court, because the sum claimed is less than £100,000.
County Court, because the estimated costs are less than £50,000.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.4: Commencing court proceedings: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A local butcher intends to bring proceedings against a competitor for making defamatory comments about the sourcing of their produce. The solicitors acting for the butcher have advised that they should expect to obtain damages of £30,000-£40,000 and a final injunction against the competitor preventing further similar statements. Should the claim be issued in the County Court or the High Court?
options: High Court, because there will be complex facts.
County Court, because the value of the claim is less than £100,000.
High Court, because the outcome of the case will attract publicity.
High Court, because all defamation claims must be brought in the High Court.
County Court, because the value of the claim is less than £50,000.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.4: Commencing court proceedings: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A company that develops computer software for medical research is in dispute with a competitor. They believe that the competitor has obtained a copy of their valuable intellectual property and is using it unlawfully to develop competing software. Which of the following is the most appropriate place to issue a claim?
options: County Court.
High Court, Admiralty Court.
High Court, Chancery Division.
High Court, Commercial Court.
High Court, King’s Bench Division.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.4: Commencing court proceedings: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A local children’s charity in Kettering is seeking a judicial review of a decision to cut funding made by the executive of their local council. The charity is asking the court to set aside the executive’s decision. They are not claiming any monetary remedy. Which of the following is the most appropriate place to issue a claim?
options: County Court, because the claim is worth less than £100,000.
High Court, Family Division, because it deals with most cases concerning children’s welfare.
High Court, Chancery Division, because it hears appeals of local County Court decisions.
High Court, King's Bench Division, because it includes the Administrative Court.
County Court, because the claim concerns a local matter.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.4: Commencing court proceedings: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A breach of contract claim between two large banks has been issued in the Commercial Court. The claim is for damages in excess of £25 million and a final injunction. The claimant’s solicitors are preparing for a hearing of an application for an interim injunction. Where should the solicitors first look for guidance on the court’s requirements for the application hearing?
options: The Chancery Guide.
The Admiralty and Commercial Courts Guide.
The Circuit Commercial Court Guide.
The Guide to the Financial List.
The King’s Bench Division Guide.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.4: Commencing court proceedings: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A newly married couple intend to sue the jeweller that provided their wedding rings. The rings were supposed to be platinum, but the couple have discovered they are white gold. In pre-action correspondence, the jeweller denies that there has been any mistake and insists the price that was quoted and paid was for the white gold rings that were supplied. The couple are now ready to issue their claim for damages. They do not know how much they may be awarded if successful, as the valuation of their rings will depend on expert evidence. Which of the following statements best describes the issue fee in this case?
options: A fixed sum payable when the claim is issued.
No issue fee is payable when the claim is issued.
The issue fee will depend on whether the claim is issued in the County Court or the High Court.
A sum based on a percentage of the estimated value of the claim, payable when the claim is issued.
A sum based on a percentage of the sum awarded at trial, with payment deferred until that time.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.4: Commencing court proceedings: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A group of three set designers work in partnership on projects for TV and film. On their last project, the production company shut down the production and kept some of their equipment and working materials. The designers want to issue a claim against the production company for unpaid fees and damages to compensate them for the loss of their property. The total value of the claim is approximately £70,000. How should the designers issue their claim?
options: Issue online using Money Claim Online.
Take or send the claim form to any County Court hearing centre.
Send a claim form to the CIvil National Business Centre.
Take or send the claim form to the County Court hearing centre nearest to the address from which they work.
Take or send the claim form to the County Court hearing centre nearest to the registered office of the production company.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.4: Commencing court proceedings: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: One month ago, a telephone service provider issued and served a claim against a customer for unpaid bills which have been due for 2 years. Last week, the telephone service provider decided to sell its rights to all existing customer debts to a debt collection company. Its contractual rights to overdue payments from customers have been assigned to the debt collection company. Which of the following statements best describes how the claim should be pursued?
options: The telephone service provider must discontinue its claim and the opportunity for the debt collection company to claim has been lost.
The telephone service provider can continue with the claim.
The debt collection company can be substituted as claimant in place of the telephone service provider.
The telephone service provider must discontinue its claim and the debt collection company can issue a new claim.
The debt collection company must be added as a claimant alongside the telephone service provider.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.4: Commencing court proceedings: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: Three business partners run a firm of financial advisers as a general partnership. Two of the partners are in dispute with a parent of the other partner, who has received a substantial amount of financial advice and agreed to pay commercial terms. However, the parent is now unwilling to pay. The two partners intend to commence a claim against the third partner’s parent for unpaid bills, rendered over the last 3 years, in the sum of £25,000 plus interest. The two partners are individual claimants. The third business partner does not want to participate in the claim against their parent. Which of the following statements best describes how or if the proceedings should progress?
options: The proceedings can go forward but only if the court grants permission.
The third business partner should be added as a defendant.
The proceedings cannot go forward because the third business partner refuses to participate.
The third business partner does not need to be a party to the proceedings.
The third business partner should be added as a claimant.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.4: Commencing court proceedings: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: The organiser of a music festival brought a claim against a company from which it leased lighting for the main stage. They claim that the lights did not conform to the agreed specifications and 20% of them were not functional. The parties engaged in protracted pre-action correspondence, but the organiser ultimately issued a claim just before the limitation deadline. It was served on the company a few days later. It has since transpired that the defendant named on the claim form was the parent company of the lighting company, named in the footer of various emails. However, the written contract was with the subsidiary company. Which of the following statements best describes how the proceedings should progress?
options: The claimant can issue a new claim against the lighting company and discontinue the claim against the parent company.
The lighting company can be substituted as defendant in place of the parent company, provided the court grants permission.
The lighting company can be substituted as defendant in place of the parent company without their consent and without permission from the court.
The lighting company can be substituted as defendant in place of the parent company but only if they both consent.
The lighting company cannot be added to the claim at this stage.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.4: Commencing court proceedings: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

disp8.5.stem: DISP8.5: Service of proceedings: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A person has issued a claim against a utility company for compensation arising from persistent interruptions to their service. They have been writing to the complaints department of the company but have not had any satisfactory response. From online searches, the person discovered a law firm that acts for the company and wrote to them directly. The law firm responded, confirming that they do act for the company but that they could add nothing more to what had been said by the company’s complaints department. However, they said any future correspondence on the matter should be directed to them. The utility company is incorporated in England with a registered office in Durham. Which of the following statements describes a valid approach to serving the claim form on the company?
options: Personal service on the complaints adviser with whom the person has been corresponding.
First class post to the law firm acting for the company.
Fax to the utility company.
Leave at the company’s registered office.
Email to the complaints department address that has been used in correspondence with the company.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.5: Service of proceedings: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A property development company has issued proceedings for negligence against a firm of architects. The firm is comprised of three architects operating as a general partnership, with a number of employed architects working for them. None of the partners were directly involved with the work that is the subject of the claim – it was done by an employee. Which of the following statements best describes how service of the claim form can be effected on the firm?
options: First class post to the home of the employee that did the work.
Email to one of the partners of the firm at their work email address, shown on their website.
Leaving it at the offices of the solicitors that acted for the firm on the contract with the property development company.
Personal service on any of the partners when out for lunch.
Email to the contact email address on the firm’s website.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.5: Service of proceedings: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A high street fashion retailer imports clothes from a manufacturer based in Malta. The terms of the contract between the parties grant non- exclusive jurisdiction over disputes to the courts of England and Wales. Malta is a contracting state to the Hague Convention of 15 November 1965 on the Service Abroad of Judicial and Extrajudicial Documents in Civil or Commercial Matters. Based on the information available, which of the following is most likely to describe an effective procedure to serve the claim form and supporting documents on the manufacturer in Malta?
options: Email the claim form to a director of the manufacturer.
Arrange with the Foreign Process Section in the High Court for transmission and service via the central appointed authority in Malta.
Send by post direct to the defendant’s address in Malta.
Send to an agent in Malta, to personally serve the claim form at the company’s address in accordance with local law.
Arrange for an agent in Malta to file the English claim form with the Maltese court and have the court serve it in accordance with local law.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.5: Service of proceedings: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A technology company has brought a claim against a former director for breach of their duties. The company alleges that the former director diverted business opportunities to a business run by their partner. The former director is resident in Egypt, but they are a British citizen. Egypt is a contracting state to the Hague Convention of 15 November 1965 on the Service Abroad of Judicial and Extrajudicial Documents in Civil or Commercial Matters. The court has granted permission to serve the claim form out of the jurisdiction. Which of the following is likely to be required as part of the procedure and mechanisms for effecting service on the defendant?
options: A translation of the relevant documents into Arabic signed by a qualified person.
An application for permission to serve by an alternative method or at an alternative place.
Direct service by post.
An application to the court in Egypt.
Service via the Foreign Process Section and the designated central authority in Egypt.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.5: Service of proceedings: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A person underwent surgery in a hospital in Manchester 1 year ago and has issued a claim for medical negligence against their surgeon. The surgeon that undertook the surgery no longer has any association with the hospital and is now resident in Italy. The parties have engaged in pre- action correspondence. The surgeon has not appointed solicitors but has confirmed that they are willing to be served using the address of a private clinic in central London, where they regularly hold consultations. Which is the most appropriate place for the claim form to be served on the surgeon?
options: The Manchester hospital because that is where the surgery took place.
The surgeon’s residential address in Italy because that is their usual residence.
The London clinic because that is a place where the surgeon carries on business in the UK, and has been given as an address for service of the proceedings.
The surgeon’s place of business in Italy because that is their principal place of business.
The surgeon’s residential address from when they lived in the jurisdiction because that is their last known residence in the jurisdiction.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.5: Service of proceedings: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A claimant is pursuing a personal injury claim against their local council. They validly served a claim form on solicitors acting for the council by fax. The fax was transmitted at 4.45pm on Thursday. What is the deemed date of service of the claim form?
options: Thursday
Friday
Saturday
Monday
Tuesday
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.5: Service of proceedings: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A company has been served with a claim form. The particulars of claim was served separately, a week later, by first class post. The covering letter enclosing the particulars of claim was dated Friday and received on Saturday. The company needs to calculate when the defence is due by reference to the deemed date of service of the particulars of claim. What is the deemed date of service of the particulars of claim?
options: Saturday, because that is the actual date of receipt.
Saturday, because that is the next day after posting.
Sunday, because that is the second day after posting.
Monday, because that is the next business day after the second day after posting.
Tuesday, because that is the second business day after posting.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.5: Service of proceedings: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A small business owner is in dispute with a key supplier based in North Wales. For commercial reasons, they have been reluctant to issue proceedings and have been engaged in ongoing pre-action correspondence and negotiations to try to resolve the dispute. The limitation period is approaching, and the business owner has been advised to issue their claim as soon as possible. They intend to serve the claim form by first class post. After issuing the claim, how long will the claimant have to serve the claim?
options: The claim form will have to be posted by 12 midnight, 4 months from the date the claim form was issued, with the particulars of claim to follow within 14 days.
The deemed date of service of the claim form will have to be no later than 12 midnight, 4 months from the date the claim form was issued, with the particulars of claim to follow within 14 days.
The claim form and particulars of claim must be received by the defendant before the limitation deadline.
The claim form and the particulars of claim will have to be posted by 12 midnight, 4 months from the date the claim form was issued.
The deemed date of service of the claim form and particulars of claim will have to be no later than 12 midnight, 4 months from the date the claim form was issued.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.5: Service of proceedings: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A prominent politician is the victim of an ongoing malicious campaign whereby false and highly defamatory allegations are being made against them on social media by an unknown person using a pseudonym. The politician has issued a defamation claim but has not been able to locate any information that would help to discover the true name, location or contact details of the individual making the defamatory statements. The politician has sought the assistance of the operator of the website, but they have confirmed that they have no identifying information for the account holder. Can the claim proceed?
options: Yes, because the court can order service by an alternative method, such as a direct message to the defendant containing a link to access the claim form.
No, because there is no information to suggest that the defendant is in the jurisdiction.
Maybe, because the court will likely ext claim form indefinitely until the necessary information can be discovered.
Yes, because, in the circumstances, the court will make an order dispensing with service.
No, because there is no physical or electronic address that the court can order as an alternative place for service.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.5: Service of proceedings: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

disp8.6.stem: DISP8.6_ Responding to a claim_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: An individual that is resident in India has been served at their home with a claim form and particulars of claim. The claim alleges that they have breached the terms of an agreement to settle a previous claim. The individual denies the claim. A response pack is enclosed with the claim form and particulars of claim and indicates that the individual has 23 days from the date of service to respond. The individual intends to defend the claim but requires more time to prepare their defence. What should the individual include in the acknowledgment of service?
options: State that they intend to contest jurisdiction.
Confirm receipt of the documents and state that confirmation of their intentions in relation to the claim will follow.
State that they intend to defend the claim and provide an address for service in England and Wales.
State that they intend to defend the claim and make a request for consent from the claimant to extend the time period for filing the defence.
State that they intend to defend the claim, provide a summary of reasons, and give an address for service in England and Wales.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.6_ Responding to a claim_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A person is being pursued by a debt collection agency due to overdue credit card payments in the sum of £40,000. A County Court claim has been issued and served. The claim form includes the particulars of claim. The person has no defence, but believes that they can clear the debt by paying it off in instalments over time. How should they respond to the claim?
options: File an acknowledgment of service indicating that they admit the claim and await a proposal from the claimant.
File an acknowledgment of service indicating that they admit the claim and use the admission form to set out a payment proposal and information concerning their financial circumstances.
Find any reason to defend the claim to buy time.
Make an application to the court for an extension of time for filing the acknowledgment of service.
Ignore the claim and allow judgment to be entered.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.6_ Responding to a claim_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A company based in Iceland has been served with a claim form and particulars of claim. The claim is for damages for breach of contract. The company denies the claim. The contract has a clause stating that all disputes shall be referred to arbitration and that Germany should be the seat of the arbitration. How should the company respond to the claim?
options: File an acknowledgment of service indicating an intention to defend the claim, because they deny the claim.
Ignore it because the English court will not take any steps in a claim over which it has no jurisdiction.
File a defence stating that the court has no jurisdiction, because that is the defence to the court claim.
Ignore it and commence arbitration in Germany because that is the correct forum for the dispute.
File an acknowledgment of service indicating that they contest jurisdiction, because they need to apply to contest jurisdiction to avoid default judgment.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.6_ Responding to a claim_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A shipbuilder in South Korea has been served with a claim form and particulars of claim. The claimant is an oil and gas company based in Aberdeen. They allege that the shipbuilder has breached a contract to deliver a new vessel by a specified date, causing substantial damage to the company. The shipbuilder disputes the claim and contests jurisdiction. The oil and gas company has ignored a variation to the contract under which the parties agreed (among other things) that, instead of the courts of England and Wales, the courts of South Korea would have exclusive jurisdiction over any disputes. The shipbuilder has filed an acknowledgment of service indicating an intention to contest jurisdiction. What further steps must the shipbuilder take?
options: Await an application from the claimant for permission to pursue the claim notwithstanding the shipbuilder’s objection.
Issue a claim in South Korea, serve it on the oil and gas company and file it with the court.
Issue an application to contest jurisdiction, let the usual date for a defence pass and take no other step in the proceedings until the application is heard.
Issue an application to contest jurisdiction and, pending a hearing, in case the application fails, file a defence by the date it is due.
Await directions from the court as to the steps the parties should take to resolve the dispute over jurisdiction.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.6_ Responding to a claim_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A bank has issued a fixed term loan to a company, repayable in 5 years, with interest accruing and payable on a monthly basis. Under the terms of the loan agreement, if two consecutive interest payments are missed, the bank can demand repayment in full. Three consecutive interest payments were missed, and the bank served a notice demanding repayment in full plus interest. The bank’s solicitors sent a letter of claim, but no response has been received. After 2 further months, the bank instructed their solicitors to issue and serve a money claim on the company. The claim form and particulars of claim were deemed served on 1 September and the bank’s solicitors filed a certificate of service with the court shortly thereafter. By 16 September, no defence, admission nor acknowledgment of service has been filed with the court. How should the bank’s solicitors go about obtaining judgment in default?
options: Issue an application for default judgment, with notice to the company.
The court will enter default judgment automatically once the deadline for an acknowledgment of service, defence or admission has passed.
File a request with the court for default judgment.
File a request with the court for default judgment. Issue an application for default judgment, without notice to the company.
Wait until 28 days have passed since deemed service of the claim, then file a request for default judgment.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.6_ Responding to a claim_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A high net worth Spanish businessperson, resident in London, hired a PR firm on a 1 year renewable contract. However, after 2 months, they stopped paying the monthly fee and stopped all communications with the firm. The PR firm issued and served a claim form and particulars of claim by post at the businessperson’s London residence. The claim is for fees due for work undertaken and damages for lost profits regarding work that would have been undertaken had the contract run its agreed term. The claim was ignored. Therefore, the PR firm filed a certificate of service and a request for judgment with the court after the 14 day period for acknowledging service or serving a defence had passed. Which of the following statements best describes the order the court is likely to make?
options: An order that the businessperson file a defence within 14 days or default judgment will be entered.
No order because the claim form and particulars of claim were served by post and there is no evidence that they have come to the attention of the businessperson.
Judgment on liability and for the specific fees claimed, with directions for determination of damages and costs.
Judgment and an order that all sums claimed in the particulars of claim are paid, plus costs.
No order because the PR firm must make an application for default judgment.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.6_ Responding to a claim_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A hairdresser in Derby has been sued for negligence because they applied the wrong product on a client’s hair, leaving the client with a portion of their head where hair will no longer grow. The client has issued a claim in the County Court for damages arising from negligence. The claim form has been served on the hairdresser by post. The claim form states that the particulars of claim are to follow. What is the next procedural step for the hairdresser?
options: File an acknowledgment of service or defence within 14 days of receipt of the claim form.
File an acknowledgment of service or defence within 14 days of the deemed date of service of the claim form.
Nothing until the particulars of claim are served.
Nothing until the particulars of claim are served. File an acknowledgment of service or defence within 28 days of the deemed date of service of the claim form.
Nothing unless a response pack was served with the claim form, in which case they should follow the deadlines stated in the response pack.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.6_ Responding to a claim_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A taxi driver who lives and works in Torquay has been sued by the company for which they work for allegedly underreporting fares. The claim form was served by a process server at the taxi driver’s home. The particulars of claim was served 7 days later by post. The taxi driver has filed an acknowledgment of service with the court stating their intention to defend the claim in full. They also intend to counterclaim for sums they claim the company has unlawfully withheld from them. If they are found liable in the company’s claim, they will seek to set-off that sum against what is due to them from the company. By when should the defence and counterclaim be filed?
options: The defence within 14 days of the date the acknowledgment of service was filed, and the counterclaim 14 days later.
Both within 28 days of the date of deemed service of the particulars of claim.
Both within 28 days of the date the acknowledgment of service was filed.
Both within 28 days of the date of deemed service of the claim form.
Both within 14 days of the date the acknowledgment of service was filed.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.6_ Responding to a claim_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: An individual resident in New Zealand has been served with a claim form and particulars of claim by a payday lending company in England. The claim alleges that they guaranteed the payment obligations of a family member under a loan agreement. The acknowledgment of service in the response pack confirms that the individual has 26 days from service of the claim form and particulars of claim to file an acknowledgment of service, a defence or admission form. The individual wishes to acknowledge service and indicate that they intend to defend the claim. When will the defence have to be filed?
options: 14 days from the date of filing the acknowledgment of service.
28 days from the date of filing the acknowledgment of service.
40 days from service of the claim form and particulars of claim.
40 days from service of the claim form and particulars of claim. 52 days from service of the claim form and particulars of claim.
54 days from service of the claim form and particulars of claim.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.6_ Responding to a claim_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A financial services firm based in Bangor, Wales, is the defendant to a claim brought by a group of former clients. The latter allege overcharging and breaches of duty concerning the use of client funds for businesses related to the firm. The claim form and particulars of claim were served at the headquarters of the firm. The firm intends to defend the claim but has to undertake an extensive investigation and interview several former employees. They estimate that they will need a total of 3 months before they will be in a position to plead a defence. The firm has acknowledged service, giving them 28 days from the deemed date of service of the particulars of claim. Which of the following best describes the firm’s options?
options: The parties can agree on unlimited extensions of time, provided they do not interfere with any scheduled hearing.
The parties can agree a further 28 days without permission and any further extensions will require permission from the court.
The parties can agree a further 28 days, but no further time will be granted.
No further time is available.
Any further extension will always require consent from the court.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.6_ Responding to a claim_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

disp8.7.stem: DISP8.7_ Statements of case_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A solicitor has been authorised by their client to sign the statement of truth in the client’s particulars of claim. The solicitor explained the statement of truth and the consequences of making a false statement of truth. Following service of the particulars of claim, the solicitors for the defendant have sent a letter pointing out a number of factual assertions in the particulars of claim that are now obviously false and must have been known by the client to be false when the particulars of claim were signed. This development has significantly damaged the claimant’s prospects of success in the case and their solicitor has advised them to seek a settlement as soon as possible. Which of the following statements best describes whether there are any other potential consequences for the claimant?
options: The maximum penalty is an adverse costs order, because the claimant has caused the defendant to incur costs unreasonably.
None, because it is the responsibility of the solicitor to verify the contents of the particulars of claim.
None, because they have not yet given evidence under oath.
None, because they did not sign the statement of truth.
Potential imprisonment, because causing a statement of truth to be made without an honest belief in its truth can lead to proceedings for contempt of court.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.7_ Statements of case_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A specialist carpentry company has issued proceedings against one of its wood suppliers. The carpentry company alleges that wood supplied was not within the contractual specifications, was sub-standard, and products manufactured with it have warped, causing them to have to refund customers on a series of projects. The carpentry company claims damages, including for its lost profits. It does not have a specific figure at this stage but believes that its losses are likely to be between £60,000 and £80,000, once more customers seek refunds and the lost profits are calculated. The claim will be issued in the County Court. On the claim form, the company has to give a statement of value. What should the company put as the statement of value?
options: “The claimant cannot say how much is likely to be recovered."
“The claimant expects to recover less than £100,000.”
“The claimant expects to recover between £60,000 and £80,000."
“The claimant expects to recover more than £50,000.”
“The claimant expects to recover more than £25,000, but not more than £100,000.”
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.7_ Statements of case_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A limited liability partnership provides financial advice to consumers. It is in dispute with an advertising agency. The agency used misleading language in adverts it placed on behalf of the LLP 2 years ago. The adverts have caused damage to the LLP’s business in lost profits over the last 2 years. The losses are currently estimated at £280,000. The LLP is preparing its claim and understands that it might not reach trial for another year. It therefore wants to ask the court to award interest on any damages awarded. As there is no contractual right to interest, the rate and time period will be up to the court. Should the LLP plead a claim for interest in the particulars of claim?
options: Yes, because a claim for interest must be pleaded and should be claimed under s 35A of the Senior Courts Act 1981.
Yes, because a claim for interest must be pleaded and should be claimed under s 69 of the County Courts Act 1984.
No, because interest will be applied automatically at a rate of 8%.
No, because interest can only be claimed if there is a contractual right to interest.
No, because the court will always consider interest when it is quantifying damages and assessing costs after trial.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.7_ Statements of case_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: An individual has been served with a claim form and particulars of claim by their former business partner. The claimant alleges that, on seven occasions, the individual made specific defamatory statements about them, which has caused substantial harm to their reputation. The defendant is unconcerned with the claim and does not want to comment on each specific alleged statement in each conversation. They deny making most (but not all) of the statements. They are confident that the witnesses will back up their version of events. They assert that none of the statements, even if all of them were made, could have caused any harm to the claimant and the claim will fail on that basis alone. Which of the following statements best describes an appropriate approach to preparing the defence?
options: The defence must respond to every allegation that the defendant believes is relevant to the case.
The defence does not need to respond to every allegation because the defendant is confident the claimant will not be able to prove their case at trial.

The defence must respond to every allegation made in the particulars of claim, because unanswered allegations will be deemed denied. Not all allegations are denied, and the defendant will need to sign a statement of truth.
The defence must respond to every allegation made in the particulars of claim, because unanswered allegations will be deemed accepted.
The defence does not need to respond to specific allegations concerning verbal discussions, because they will be the subject of cross- examination of witnesses at trial.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.7_ Statements of case_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A claimant has brought a claim against a surveyor, alleging negligence in relation to a property purchase. In the surveyor’s defence, they deny liability and raise various matters that were not addressed by the claimant in the particulars of claim. Does the claimant have to serve a reply?
options: Yes, because the reply must respond to every allegation made in the defence and any allegations to which the claimant does not respond are deemed denied.
No, because a reply to a defence in not mandatory.

No, because a reply to a defence in not mandatory. Yes, because the reply must respond to any positive allegation made in the defence and any positive allegations to which the claimant does not respond are deemed admitted.
Yes, because the reply must respond to every allegation made in the defence and any allegations to which the claimant does not respond are deemed admitted.
No, because there is no counterclaim.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.7_ Statements of case_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A wealthy celebrity actor has, over many years, been given financial advice by a general partnership of three financial advisers. They deal mainly with one partner but are a client of the partnership. The actor has been recently audited by HMRC and has been ordered to pay a large sum in additional tax and penalties. The actor has issued a claim against their main contact at the firm, alleging negligence. The defendant has pointed out that they are one of three partners in the firm and therefore all three partners or the firm itself should be named as defendant. The actor has nonetheless pursued their claim against only one partner and served them with particulars of claim. Which of the following statements best describes the appropriate procedure for the defendant to ensure any claim is shared between the partners of the firm?
options: They must await the outcome of the case before there is any cause of action for a contribution from the other partners.
Issue and serve a Part 20 claim against the other two partners.
Issue and serve a Part 20 claim against the other two partners. Issue separate proceedings against the other two partners.
Defend the claim on the basis that it is invalid because the claimant has served only one of three partners.
Counterclaim against the other two partners.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.7_ Statements of case_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A lender has issued a claim against a small business to which sums were loaned under a fixed term loan agreement. The lender alleges that the borrower is in default of its payment obligations, which has given the lender a right to terminate the agreement and claim the debt in full. The borrower denies the claim, on the basis that the defaults in payment do not yet give rise to a right to terminate. The borrower blames their cashflow constraints on a customer not making payment for a large project, in breach of their payment terms. They have engaged in pre-action correspondence, but no resolution has been reached. Which of the following statements best describes an appropriate approach for the borrower to pursue their claim against their non-paying customer?
options: Issue a new claim against the customer and pursue it in separate proceedings.
Apply to the court to add the customer as a co-defendant to the claim.
Issue a Part 20 claim against the customer after the lender’s reply to the defence.
Ask the lender to add the customer as a co-defendant to the claim.
Issue a Part 20 claim against the customer when the defence is filed.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.7_ Statements of case_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A farmer is the defendant to a claim alleging a breach of a contract. The particulars of claim state that a verbal contract for the sale of farm animals was reached between the parties “around April [last year]”. It does not include any details of where the agreement was reached or what was said. The claimant alleges that, in breach of contract, the farmer has not delivered the animals within a reasonable period. The farmer did various deals with the claimant early last year. However, they are certain that the alleged contract was never agreed. An extension of time for the defence has already been granted, so the deadline is not imminent. Which of the following statements best describes an appropriate next step?
options: Make an application to the court for an order that the claimant provide specific further information concerning the alleged agreement.

Make an application to the court for an order that the claimant re-plead the whole particulars of claim with all information available to them concerning all alleged discussions around April last year.
Send a written request for specific further information concerning the alleged agreement.
Inform the claimant that the defence will not be served until better information is provided.
Send a written request for a witness statement from the claimant with full details of all alleged discussions around April last year.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.7_ Statements of case_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A surveyor is a defendant to a claim for negligence by a property investor. The claimant alleges that the surveyor gave them an unrealistically high valuation of £12 million for a commercial property. On the basis of the valuation, the investor acquired the property at auction for £10 million. However, when seeking to mortgage the property, two independent surveyors have provided valuations of £8 million and £8.5 million. The surveyor has just served their defence, in which they deny negligence and assert that they relied on “data from other sales of comparable properties in the area” and “a report by a leading estate agent in the area published 6 months before the valuation”. Which of the following statements best describes whether the claimant can obtain clarification of the basis for the defendant’s valuation at this stage of the proceedings?
options: They can serve a request for further information and obtain a copy of the report, but not any other documents.
They will have to wait until disclosure and witness statements.
They can serve a request for further information but will have to wait on disclosure to obtain a copy of the report and other documents the surveyor used.
They are entitled to a copy of the report but will have to wait on disclosure and witness statements for any other details.
They are entitled to copies of the report and documents containing the data relied upon for the valuation.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.7_ Statements of case_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A 25% shareholder in a company is in dispute with the other three shareholders. The cause of action is unfair prejudice, and the claimant shareholder is seeking an order that their shares be acquired by the majority shareholders at a fair value. The claimant shareholder alleges that the other three shareholders unfairly prejudiced them by removing them as a director and generally excluding them from decision-making in the business, contrary to what was agreed when the company was established. The parties have completed disclosure and exchanged relevant documents. The defendants have disclosed a series of emails between them which show that they paid dividends to themselves but not to the claimant. This also would amount to unfair prejudice. Which of the following statements best describes how the claimant shareholder should pursue this issue?
options: Seek consent or permission to amend their statement of case to add the unlawful dividends, because that is an additional fact on which the cause of action should be based.
Continue with the claim and cross-examine the defendants on the matter at trial, because the dividends are facts in support of the existing cause of action.
Make a request for further information about the dividends, because the other shareholders’ response will be a statement of case.
Issue new unfair prejudice proceedings in connection with the dividend payments, because new facts cannot be pleaded after disclosure.
File and serve an amended statement of case including the dividends issue, because consent or permission to add new facts in support of an existing cause of action is not required.
questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.source: DISP8.7_ Statements of case_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A property developer sells a piece of land. Included in the contract of sale is a clause confirming that an easement will be granted on completion to allow the buyer to install a gas pipe over the property developer’s retained land. The buyer installs the pipe. The transfer from the property developer to the buyer did not mention the right to install the pipe. Which of the following statements best describes the interest that the buyer may have in relation to the pipe?
options: The buyer has no interest because the transfer did not contain the right to install the pipe.
The buyer has a legal easement to install the pipe.
The buyer has an equitable easement to install the pipe.
The buyer has a personal right to install the pipe.
The buyer has a licence to install the pipe.
questions.subject: Land Law
questions.source: LAND4.1: Nature of land: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A person purchased a large manor house and had the gardens landscaped. A central feature of the landscaping project was the positioning of a large statue of a mermaid next to the lake in the garden. The mermaid was made of concrete and thus did not need to be affixed to a surface as the weight of the statue was sufficient to keep it in place. A person sold the manor house and took the mermaid statue with them on completion. The contract of sale made no reference to the mermaid statue. Which of the following statements best describes whether a person was entitled to remove the mermaid statue?
options: Yes, because it was the person’s personal property.
No, because the mermaid statue was placed on the property to improve it and had become a fixture.
Yes, because the mermaid statue was not fixed to the ground and was thus a fitting which the person was entitled to remove.
Yes, because the mermaid statue was a “chose in action”.
No, because the contract did not contain a reference to the mermaid statue.
questions.subject: Land Law
questions.source: LAND4.1: Nature of land: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: Person A offers to sell to a friend (Person B) the right to take fish from a lake belonging to a neighbour. Person B is worried because A does not own the lake. What interest is Person A likely to hold?
options: Person A is likely to hold an easement.
Person A is likely to hold an equitable easement.
Person A is likely to hold a rent-charge.
Person A is likely to hold a profit a prendre appurtenant.
Person A is likely to hold a profit a prendre in gross.
questions.subject: Land Law
questions.source: LAND4.1: Nature of land: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A farmer recently purchased an area of moorland upon which wild deer roam freely. The farmer is pleased because their cattle business is faltering and they want to catch the deer and keep them in an enclosure to breed them for commercial purposes. Which of the following statements best describes whether the farmer can do as they wish with the deer?
options: Yes, provided that the farmer obtains the appropriate licence to do so.
No, the farmer cannot enclose and breed the deer as they do not own them, but the farmer can hunt them.
Yes, the farmer can do as they wish with the deer because the deer fall within the definition of “land”.
No, the farmer cannot do as they wish with the deer because the deer are “fittings” and do not pass with the land.
No, the farmer cannot keep the deer in an enclosure because the deer do not fall within the definition of “land”.
questions.subject: Land Law
questions.source: LAND4.1: Nature of land: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: Two landowners own adjoining pieces of land. Title to both pieces of land is unregistered. They agree that one will grant the other a right of way over their land to gain access to the public highway. They enter into a deed of easement. One party forgot to sign the deed and the other party signed it but their signature was not witnessed. The landowner with the benefit of the right of way exercised the right for four years, until the neighbouring landowner said that they could no longer exercise the right of way. Which of the following statements best describes the position of the landowners in relation to the right of way?
options: A legal right has not been created but a right in equity has arisen, which should be protected by registration of a D(ii) land charge.
The status of the deed of easement is irrelevant because the landowner has an overriding interest.
Whether the deed of easement is legal or equitable is not relevant because the landowner has acquired a right by prescription.
A legal right has been created and the deed of easement should be placed with the landowners’ unregistered title deeds.
A legal right has not been created but a right in equity has arisen, which should be protected by registration of a D(iii) land charge.
questions.subject: Land Law
questions.source: LAND4.1: Nature of land: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A lawyer is acting for a client who is selling their house. The title to the seller’s house is registered at HM Land Registry. The seller is not retaining any land. Which document will transfer the legal title of the house from the seller to the buyer on completion?
options: A transfer of whole.
An assent.
A lease.
A transfer of part.
A conveyance.
questions.subject: Land Law
questions.source: LAND4.1: Nature of land: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A seller has agreed to sell their house and garden. On the day of completion, the buyer attends the property to find the seller removing the plants and shrubs from the garden. When asked what they were doing, the seller told the buyer that they wanted them for their new garden. Is the seller permitted to remove the plants and shrubs?
options: No, because the seller is obliged to leave the property in the same condition as it was at exchange of contracts.
Yes, because the plants and shrubs do not form part of the land and are not included in the sale.
Yes, provided that the seller has indicated that they are taking the plants and shrubs on the fittings and contents form.
Yes, because the plants and shrubs are personal property and can be removed by the seller.
No, because the plants and shrubs form part of the surface of the land and are included in the sale.
questions.subject: Land Law
questions.source: LAND4.1: Nature of land: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A seller has exchanged contracts for the sale of their property. The contract included a fittings and contents form, upon which the seller indicated that they were removing six holly bushes that they had planted in the garden at the property. After completion, the seller received a letter from the buyer demanding the return of the holly bushes, stating that they were not entitled to remove them from the property. Is the buyer correct?
options: No, the seller can remove the holly bushes because the fittings and contents form forms part of the contract.
Yes, because the holly bushes are personal property and can be removed on completion.
Yes, due to the degree of annexation, the holly bushes form part of the land.
Yes, because the holly bushes form part of the land and must be left at the property on completion.
No, because the property must be left in the same condition as it was on exchange of contracts.
questions.subject: Land Law
questions.source: LAND4.1: Nature of land: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A seller has exchanged contracts to sell a property. There is a large shed in the back garden which is bolted to a concrete slab in the garden. On the day of completion, the buyer arrives at the property to discover that the seller has removed the shed and has tidied up the concrete slab and filled in the holes. The buyer tells the seller that they were expecting the shed to be left at the property. The seller tells the buyer that they were allowed to remove the shed. Is the seller correct?
options: Yes, because the seller has carefully removed the shed and has made good the damage caused.
No, because the shed is bolted to the land and is thus a fixture which will pass with the sale of the land.
No, because the property must be left in the same condition as it was on exchange of contracts.
Yes, because the shed is not attached to the land by concrete foundations and it is only a fitting which will not pass with the sale of the land.
No, because the seller has not made good the damage caused to the property by the removal of the shed.
questions.subject: Land Law
questions.source: LAND4.1: Nature of land: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A registered proprietor of a freehold estate has borrowed money from a bank, which appears on the charges register of title as a first legal charge. They have also just completed a deed of easement containing a right of way which benefits their land, which also appears on the charges register. The property register of the title contains a right to use a water pipe in favour of the registered proprietor’s land. All of the rights are legal in nature. How are these interests best described?
options: Personal interests.
Overriding interests.
Equitable interests.
Concurrent interests.
Leasehold interests.
questions.subject: Land Law
questions.source: LAND4.1: Nature of land: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

land4.2.stem: LAND4.2: Title to land: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: An unmarried couple (A and B) are splitting up. The house, which they have lived in as their home, is owned in the sole name of A. B did not contribute to the purchase price of the property. B is worried that A might sell the house and want B to move out. Which of the following statements best describes B’s legal position?
options: B need not be concerned as B will have an overriding interest.
B should register a class F land charge against the title to the property to protect B’s right of occupation.
B should register a home rights’ notice against the title to the property to protect B’s right of occupation.
B should make an application to court for a share of the proceeds of sale.
B should remain in occupation of the property but does not have an interest that is capable of protection.
questions.subject: Land Law
questions.source: LAND4.2: Title to land: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A landlord and tenant entered into a new 10-year lease of commercial premises. On conclusion of the transaction, the tenant’s lawyer paid the relevant stamp duty land tax on the lease, submitted a bill to their client, closed the file and sent the lease to their client. The lawyer took no further steps. What action should the lawyer take to perfect the title on completion of the lease?
options: The lawyer should have served notice of the lease on the landlord.
The lawyer should have registered the lease at HM Land Registry.
The lawyer should have ensured that the tenant took a share in the management company.
The lawyer should have served notice of the mortgage on the landlord.
The lawyer should have registered the lease at HM Revenue and Customs.
questions.subject: Land Law
questions.source: LAND4.2: Title to land: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A couple buy a property together and their lawyer advises them to hold the beneficial interest as tenants in common. Which of the following best describes how their beneficial interest should be protected on the register of title?
options: A notice in the Proprietorship Register.
A restriction in the Property Register.
A restriction in the Charges Register.
A restriction in the Proprietorship Register.
A notice in the Charges Register.
questions.subject: Land Law
questions.source: LAND4.2: Title to land: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A freehold property owner is considering granting a lease of the property to a prospective tenant. The owner is aware that they will have to obtain a plan of the premises if the lease is to be registered under the Land Registration Act 2002. In relation to the grant of a lease, which of the following triggers registration of the leasehold interest?
options: A lease of more than 21 years.
A lease of more than 7 years.
A lease of more than 3 years.
A lease of more than 15 years.
A lease of more than 10 years.
questions.subject: Land Law
questions.source: LAND4.2: Title to land: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A lawyer is acting for a client who is purchasing a leasehold property, with an unregistered lease which has a residue of 22 years to run. Is the lease registrable at HM Land Registry on completion?
options: Yes, because a lease with more than seven years to run on assignment is registrable.
Yes, because an unregistered lease is registrable, irrespective of the number of years left on the lease on assignment.
No, because an unregistered lease with fewer than 21 years to run on assignment is not registrable.
No, because an unregistered lease is not registrable.
Yes, because an unregistered lease with more than 21 years to run on assignment is registrable.
questions.subject: Land Law
questions.source: LAND4.2: Title to land: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A lawyer is acting for a client who is selling their property which has an unregistered title. The lawyer has obtained the title deeds. To adequately deduce title, how far back should the seller’s title go?
options: 15 years.
7 years.
3 years.
10 years.
21 years.
questions.subject: Land Law
questions.source: LAND4.2: Title to land: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A landowner wishes to sell their farm but discovers that their unregistered title deeds have been lost. The landowner consults their lawyer for advice and is told that the lawyer can make an application for registration at HM Land Registry, based on lost title deeds. What class of title is the land registry likely to grant?
options: Good leasehold title.
Freehold title.
Title absolute.
Qualified title.
Possessory title.
questions.subject: Land Law
questions.source: LAND4.2: Title to land: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: 3 years. 10 years. 21 years.
options: HM Land Registry will register the title to the lease as a freehold title.
HM Land Registry will register the title to the lease with good leasehold title.
HM Land Registry will register the title to the lease with title absolute.
HM Land Registry will note the lease on the freehold title.
HM Land Registry will reject the application because the lease is not substantively registrable as it is for less than 21 years.
